Pallu
PAL-loo
proper noun
Hebrew Pallu (H6396), distinguished or wonderful — from pala (H6381), to be marvellous, to be set apart as extraordinary; written Phallu at Genesis 46:9.

Biblical Definition

Pallu was the second son of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, and head of one of the four Reubenite families — the Palluites (Gen 46:9, where the Authorized Version spells it Phallu; Exo 6:14; Num 26:5; 1Ch 5:3). He went down into Egypt with Jacob's household and his line came out at the exodus. Numbers records that his son was Eliab, and Eliab's sons were Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram — that Dathan and Abiram, which were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah (Num 26:9). So the house named wonderful produced, within two generations, two of the ringleaders of the rebellion that the earth swallowed. The irony is not accidental to the way Scripture tells Reuben's story. Reuben was the firstborn with every natural advantage — the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power — and lost it by instability (Gen 49:3-4). A tribe of distinguished beginnings and forfeited inheritance is the standing warning of the Pentateuch that birthright is not character, and that a good name handed down is a trust rather than a possession.

Origin & Era

Second son of Reuben and head of the family of the Palluites; his name means distinguished or wonderful.

PALLU, Hebrew Pallu, distinguished, wonderful; written Phallu at Genesis 46:9.

The second son of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel.

Head of the family of the Palluites, one of the four families of Reuben.

He went down into Egypt in the household of Jacob.

His grandsons Dathan and Abiram rebelled with Korah against Moses.

Key Scripture

Gen 46:9 — "And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi."

Num 26:5 — "Reuben, the eldest son of Israel: the children of Reuben; Hanoch, of whom cometh the family of the Hanochites: of Pallu, the family of the Palluites:"

Num 26:8 — "And the sons of Pallu; Eliab."

1Ch 5:3 — "The sons, I say, of Reuben the firstborn of Israel were, Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi."

Modern Corruption

A distinguished name is mistaken for a settled standing; Scripture makes every generation answer for itself.

expand to see more

Covenant privilege is easily misread as covenant safety. Israel made that mistake constantly — We have Abraham to our father (Mat 3:9) — and John the Baptist answered that God is able of stones to raise up children unto Abraham. The house of Pallu had privilege in abundance: descent from the firstborn of Israel, a name meaning distinguished, a place in the households that came out of Egypt under the blood of the lamb. Two generations later its most famous members are Dathan and Abiram, standing at their tent doors in open defiance of the man God had sent.

The corollary is the sober doctrine of the visible church. Baptism does not regenerate; a Christian household does not guarantee a Christian child; membership is not the same as union with Christ. They are not all Israel, which are of Israel (Rom 9:6). What the privilege does is set a child under the means of grace — preaching, ordinance, family instruction — which God ordinarily uses and which no child may presume upon. The principle to recover is that every generation must be converted for itself, and that a name like Pallu is an obligation rather than an inheritance.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Pallu (H6396), from pala (H6381), to be wonderful, marvellous, set apart as extraordinary.

expand to see more

Hebrew pala (H6381) — to be marvellous, wonderful, beyond ordinary; Is any thing too hard for the LORD? (Gen 18:14) uses this root.

Hebrew Pallu (H6396) — second son of Reuben; Genesis 46:9, Exodus 6:14, Numbers 26:5, 1 Chronicles 5:3.

Hebrew pele (H6382) — a wonder, a marvel; the Messiah is called Wonderful (Isa 9:6).

Hebrew bekor (H1060) — firstborn; Reuben's station, forfeited by instability (Gen 49:3-4).

Hebrew mishpachah (H4940) — a family, a clan; the Palluites as one of the four families of Reuben.
